clauses.title: Security Deposit
clauses.summary: The security deposit of $5,000 is excessive — many jurisdictions cap deposits at 1-2 months' rent. No interest accrual or return timeline is specified.
clauses.recommendation: Negotiate the deposit down to one month's rent ($2,500) and require it be held in a separate interest-bearing account with a defined return timeline.
clauses.suggestedRewrite: Tenant shall pay a security deposit equal to one month's rent ($2,500), to be held in a separate interest-bearing account. Landlord shall return the deposit within 30 days of lease termination, minus any itemised deductions for damages beyond normal wear and tear.
clauses.details: Original text: "Tenant shall pay a security deposit of $5,000 to be held by Landlord for the duration of the lease."

clauses.title: Late Payment Penalty
clauses.summary: A $250 late fee on $2,500 rent is a 10% penalty, which may exceed legal limits in many jurisdictions. The 3-day grace period is very short.
clauses.recommendation: Negotiate a grace period of at least 10 days and a late fee capped at 5% of monthly rent or $50, whichever is less.
clauses.suggestedRewrite: If rent is not received by the 10th of each month, a late fee of $50 or 5% of the monthly rent (whichever is less) will be charged. Tenant shall receive a written notice before any late fee is applied.
clauses.details: Original text: "If rent is not received by the 3rd of each month, a late fee of $250 will be charged immediately."

clauses.title: Maintenance Responsibilities
clauses.summary: Shifting ALL maintenance responsibility to the tenant is unusual and potentially unenforceable. Landlords are typically required by law to maintain structural elements and essential systems.
clauses.recommendation: Split responsibilities: landlord handles structural and major systems, tenant handles minor upkeep and negligence-caused damage.
clauses.suggestedRewrite: Landlord shall be responsible for all structural repairs and maintenance of plumbing, electrical, and HVAC systems. Tenant shall be responsible for minor upkeep and any damage caused by tenant negligence.
clauses.details: Original text: "Tenant shall be responsible for all repairs and maintenance of the premises, including plumbing, electrical, and HVAC systems."

clauses.title: Early Termination
clauses.summary: A blanket prohibition on early termination with no mitigation requirement is harsh and may not hold up in court. Many jurisdictions require landlords to mitigate damages.
clauses.recommendation: Propose an early termination option with 60 days' notice and a reasonable termination fee of two months' rent.
clauses.suggestedRewrite: Tenant may terminate this lease early with 60 days' written notice and payment of a termination fee equal to two months' rent. Landlord shall make reasonable efforts to re-let the premises to offset remaining rent obligations.
clauses.details: Original text: "Tenant may not terminate this lease early under any circumstances. All remaining rent becomes immediately due upon vacating."

clauses.title: Entry Rights
clauses.summary: Entry without notice violates tenant privacy rights in virtually every jurisdiction. Most areas require 24-48 hours' notice except in emergencies.
clauses.recommendation: Insist on at least 24 hours' written notice for non-emergency entry, with entries during reasonable hours only.
clauses.suggestedRewrite: Landlord shall provide at least 24 hours' written notice before entering the premises, except in cases of genuine emergency. Entry shall occur during reasonable hours (9am-6pm) and only for legitimate purposes (inspections, repairs, showings).
clauses.details: Original text: "Landlord may enter the premises at any time without notice for any reason."

clauses.title: Rent Increase
clauses.summary: Allowing unlimited rent increases with only 15 days' notice provides no stability for the tenant. In a 12-month lease, rent should be fixed for the term.
clauses.recommendation: Lock rent for the lease term. If increases on renewal are allowed, require 90 days' notice and cap at CPI or 3%.
clauses.suggestedRewrite: Rent shall remain fixed for the duration of the lease term. Any rent increase upon renewal shall require 90 days' written notice and shall not exceed the greater of 3% or the local CPI increase.
clauses.details: Original text: "Landlord reserves the right to increase rent at any time with 15 days' notice."

clauses.title: Liability and Insurance
clauses.summary: A blanket liability waiver for the landlord is likely unenforceable. Landlords cannot contract away negligence liability for conditions they control.
clauses.recommendation: Change to shared liability: each party responsible for their own negligence. Require landlord to maintain property insurance.
clauses.suggestedRewrite: Each party shall be responsible for liabilities arising from their own negligence. Landlord shall maintain property insurance. Tenant is encouraged to obtain renter's insurance for personal property.
clauses.details: Original text: "Tenant assumes all liability for injuries occurring on the premises, regardless of cause. Landlord shall not be held liable for any damages."

clauses.title: Lease Duration
clauses.summary: A standard 12-month lease term is normal and reasonable.

clauses.title: Monthly Rent
clauses.summary: The rent amount and due date are clearly stated, which is standard practice.

clauses.title: Utilities
clauses.summary: While tenants commonly pay utilities, the clause should specify which utilities exist and clarify that landlord pays for common area utilities in multi-unit buildings.
clauses.recommendation: Clarify utility split: tenant pays electricity/gas/internet, landlord pays water/sewer/trash.
clauses.suggestedRewrite: Tenant shall be responsible for electricity, gas, and internet. Landlord shall be responsible for water, sewer, and trash collection. Tenant shall set up utility accounts in their name within 5 days of move-in.

clauses.title: Pets Policy
clauses.summary: A blanket pet ban with 'approval' is vague — the criteria for approval should be stated. Also, emotional support animals may need to be accommodated under fair housing laws.
clauses.recommendation: Request defined pet criteria and a reasonableness clause for approval. Add service/emotional support animal accommodation.
clauses.suggestedRewrite: Tenant may keep up to 2 domestic pets with prior written approval (not to be unreasonably withheld). A pet deposit of $300 shall be required. Reasonable accommodations for service and emotional support animals as required by law.

clauses.title: Subletting
clauses.summary: Standard subletting restriction, but 'consent' should include a reasonableness requirement so the landlord can't arbitrarily refuse.
clauses.recommendation: Add 'not to be unreasonably withheld' language to the consent requirement.
clauses.suggestedRewrite: Tenant may not sublet or assign the lease without prior written consent of the Landlord, which shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed.

clauses.title: Quiet Enjoyment
clauses.summary: A standard quiet enjoyment clause that protects the tenant's right to use the property peacefully.

clauses.title: Parking
clauses.summary: Clear, fair allocation of parking at no extra cost is reasonable.

gapAnalysis.suggestion: Add a move-in/move-out inspection checklist to be completed jointly by both parties, with photos, to prevent disputes over security deposit deductions.
Add a mediation or arbitration clause requiring good-faith negotiation before either party can file a lawsuit.
Add a clause requiring the tenant to maintain renter's insurance and naming the landlord as an interested party.
